recent_posts.title: A guided meditation session for developers using programming metaphors
recent_posts.summary: A guided meditation and mindfulness session written specifically for software developers, using programming metaphors (stack, read-only mode, log entries, tab management, graceful restart) to help developers pause, breathe, and decompress from the mental load of coding work. The session walks through breathing exercises, a body scan, and thought-observation techniques before gently returning the listener to their work.

recent_posts.title: Astro's new Fonts API
recent_posts.summary: Astro's new experimental Fonts API solves common web font headaches including privacy concerns (no user IP sent to Google), layout shift, lack of type safety, and unnecessary font downloads. The API downloads fonts at build time rather than runtime, keeping them local to your site. Configuration happens in astro.config.mjs with support for multiple font providers (Google, Fontsource, Adobe, Bunny, local, npm), CSS variables, specific weights/styles/subsets, local fonts, and variable fonts. An optimized fallback feature reduces cumulative layout shift by generating fallback fonts that closely match the target font's metrics.

recent_posts.title: NEW Astro Component Starter
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of the new Astro Component Starter built with Cloud Cannon, aimed at agencies and freelancers managing non-technical clients. The starter provides a Git-based Astro project with zero JavaScript by default for performance, paired with Cloud Cannon's visual CMS editing experience. Developers retain full control over components, theming via design tokens, and which fields clients can edit. The tutorial covers installation, project structure, theming, connecting to Cloud Cannon, the two-way Git sync workflow, and building custom components using an in-docs component builder that generates the required Astro, inputs, and structure files.

recent_posts.title: Astro 6 new features overview including fonts API, live collections, CSP and route caching
recent_posts.summary: Astro 6.0 has been released with several notable features graduating from experimental to stable. The Fonts API now supports local fonts, Google Fonts, and Fontsource with a unified component-based API. Live Content Collections enable real-time data fetching at request time, complementing the existing static build-time collections. Content Security Policy support is now stable and built-in by default, with a full configuration API including custom hashing algorithms and directives. Under the hood, the dev server has been refactored for better dev/production parity, especially for Cloudflare deployments. New experimental features include a Rust-based compiler for speed improvements, queued rendering (a two-pass approach replacing recursive rendering, planned as default in Astro 7), and a platform-agnostic route caching API using web-standard cache semantics. The release also upgrades to Zod 4 and requires Node 20+.

recent_posts.title: How to add smooth navbar view transitions in Astro
recent_posts.summary: A practical walkthrough of adding animated navbar navigation using View Transitions in Astro. The approach uses an absolutely positioned span element with a transition name to create a smooth sliding indicator between nav items, rather than animating the entire page. The browser handles diffing between old and new states automatically once elements share the same transition name across pages.

recent_posts.title: My notes app: Git, Claude, Markdown
recent_posts.summary: A walkthrough of Scratch, a lightweight Markdown text editor built largely through vibe coding with Claude and Cursor. The tool syncs notes via Git, integrates Claude Code for AI-assisted task organization, and can be installed via Homebrew. The author uses it as a daily scratchpad alongside Obsidian and iA Writer, appreciating its simplicity, Git sync, and built-in AI commands for organizing thoughts into task lists.

recent_posts.title: Micro-interactions still matter
recent_posts.summary: A short CSS tutorial demonstrating how to create polished micro-interactions using just four lines of CSS. The technique combines hover background color changes using OKLCH color with opacity, a box shadow for visual depth, a scale transform on active/click state, and a custom linear easing function for a 'squishy' feel. The box shadow approach is preferred over background-with-padding because it doesn't disrupt document flow, allowing the squish animation to work smoothly. CSS nesting, modern scale property, and easing generators like Easing Wizard are used throughout.

recent_posts.title: My favorite way to author blogs in Astro
recent_posts.summary: Astro Editor is a markdown writing tool designed specifically for Astro projects, inspired by iA Writer's design philosophy. The editor offers features like focus mode, syntax highlighting for parts of speech, MDX component embedding, smart image handling, and auto-detection of blog content. It supports both markdown and MDX files, includes a command palette, and provides a distraction-free writing experience separate from traditional IDEs. While some features like component imports and prop type handling need refinement, the tool is actively maintained by an indie developer and available via Homebrew.

top_posts.title: My new favorite way to use git
top_posts.summary: Git is a powerful tool with a steep learning curve, especially when using the command line interface. Lazy Git offers a graphical interface within the CLI, making it easier to manage Git tasks without memorizing commands. The post discusses the installation on Mac OS via Homebrew and showcases basic functionalities like staging, committing, and stashing changes. It emphasizes the speed and efficiency Lazy Git brings to the table for developers.

top_posts.title: Favorite New Tailwind Extension
top_posts.summary: Fluid Tailwind is a new plugin that leverages the CSS clamp function to allow smooth transitions of values like padding, margin, and text sizes within Tailwind CSS. This plugin simplifies writing Tailwind classes and enhances UX by providing fluid transitions between values. The post also guides on setting up and configuring the plugin properly to work with Tailwind's default settings.

top_posts.title: Starwind UI: shadcn/ui for Astro
top_posts.summary: Starwind UI is a new user interface framework for Astro, created by one of Astro's co-creators, Nate Moore. It uses Astro components and vanilla JavaScript, allowing easy installation and customization. The framework includes various components like buttons, avatars, tabs, and tooltips. It integrates seamlessly with Tailwind CSS and supports event handling and accessibility features. Users can update and delete components while customizing the styles and behavior.

top_posts.title: THE VSCode extension for design systems
top_posts.summary: Enhance your design workflow in VSCode by using the CSS Var Complete extension to leverage CSS variables. This extension provides intellisense support for CSS variables, making it easier to access and use design tokens directly in your CSS files. Learn how to set up project-specific or global settings to automatically prompt collaborators to install the extension, ensuring a smooth development process.

top_posts.title: Modern JavaScript TODO app
top_posts.summary: A comprehensive tutorial for building a todo application using vanilla HTML, CSS, and JavaScript. Covers CRUD operations, local storage for data persistence, modern CSS features like custom properties and nesting, accessibility best practices including ARIA labels and screen reader support, custom events for UI rendering, and creating styled custom checkboxes. The tutorial emphasizes separation of concerns between data management and UI rendering while maintaining semantic HTML structure.
